question.prompt: Let \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) be three distinct one-digit numbers. What is the maximum value of the sum of the roots of the equation \((x - a)(x - b)\) \(+ (x - b)(x - c) = 0?\)

solutions.explanation:
Both terms contain \(x-b\), so factoring out this common factor reveals the roots directly:
\[
(x-b)\bigl((x-a)+(x-c)\bigr)
=(x-b)(2x-a-c)=0.
\]
A product is zero exactly when at least one factor is zero. Thus the two roots, counting a repeated root twice if necessary, are \(b\) and \((a+c)/2\). Their sum is
\[
S=b+\frac{a+c}{2}=\frac{a+b+c+b}{2}.
\]
The three distinct one-digit numbers have sum at most \(9+8+7=24\), and \(b\le9\). Consequently,
\[
S\le\frac{24+9}{2}=16.5.
\]
Both bounds can hold at once: take \(b=9\), \(a=7\), and \(c=8\). The roots are then \(9\) and \(7.5\), whose sum is \(16.5\). Therefore the maximum is \(16.5\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutions.title: Expose the roots and bound their sum
